hook_text: Sailors called it the Cape of Storms. A king renamed it the Cape of Good Hope. Why?
clip_script: Cape Point, wind and huge waves. For decades, Portuguese ships crept down Africa's west coast, a little further each voyage. Around 1486, a padrão was placed on the coast of Namibia. In 1488, Dias was blown south in a storm, and rounded the tip of Africa. The route was clear: Lisbon, down the Atlantic, around the Cape, up the east coast, across the Indian Ocean to India. A stormy cape, but full of good hope for trade.
visual_style: Whiteboard map of Africa with a dotted line creeping down the west coast year by year, curling around the Cape and across to India.
mood: Stormy and determined, like a long journey finally breaking through.
pacing: Slow, stepwise progress down the coast, a burst of storm at the Cape, then a smooth line to India.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw the sea route from Lisbon to India on a map.
